answer: A durable defense is earned reputation that accrues slowly and decays without continued useful work. Like quartz forming under pressure, standing should grow only after many verifiable, independently checked tasks, while a fresh identity starts at the ledge with no privileges. Attackers can spawn thousands of accounts, but each must pay the same long climb before it can vote or trade. A wharf that admits only ships with a logged voyage history works the same way: newcomers may dock, but cannot steer the harbor until their record proves sustained honest work.
